claims.claim: In a controlled component ablation on a FROZEN local 7B (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, HotpotQA distractor, n=5000), the iterative retrieve-reason LOOP is the single dominant agentic primitive: removing it costs -7.1 EM / -7.6 F1 (p<0.001), while a fixed 2-step loop captures ~95% of the gain of 5 steps (-0.3 EM vs full). Authors' verdict: 'most of the gain comes from running a short retrieval loop, not from adaptive routing or from many iterations.'
claims.source: Dissecting Agentic RAG: A Component Ablation for Multi-Hop QA with a Local 7B Model, arXiv:2606.21553, 2026 [OPENED html]
claims.relevance: Directly sizes our levers: a FIXED short loop is near-ceiling, so an RL-learned stopping/iteration policy is a marginal step-3 lever, not the main prize.

claims.claim: In the same 7B ablation, the classic 'agentic' sub-primitives each contribute only ~1-2 EM: query decomposition -1.4 EM, cross-encoder rerank -1.7 EM, adaptive routing (vs hybrid-only) -1.8 EM; dense-only vs sparse-only vs adaptive differed by only +-0.2 EM. Reflection/verification had 'surprisingly limited contribution' on this model.
claims.source: Dissecting Agentic RAG, arXiv:2606.21553, 2026 [OPENED — rerank/decompose/route numbers from html table; reflect/verify 'minimal' from pdf-pass summary, lower certainty]
claims.relevance: On small models the marquee primitives (route/rewrite/decompose/rerank/reflect/verify) are individually small; caution against over-investing training-free RL in any one on the mock. Open whether a 30B omni model amplifies verify/reflect.

claims.claim: RAG-MCP does tool-registry retrieval by keeping an external vector index of MCP/tool metadata and semantic-searching top-k per query, injecting only the winner's description. Accuracy 43.13% vs 18.20% keyword vs 13.62% naive-all-tools; prompt tokens cut >50% (1084 vs 2133); but success degrades beyond ~100 tools in the 1-1100 stress test.
claims.source: RAG-MCP: Mitigating Prompt Bloat in LLM Tool Selection via RAG, arXiv:2505.03275, 2025 [OPENED html]
claims.relevance: Our faiss KB can hold tool/function descriptions as one grain; a FIXED tool-retrieval primitive is directly reusable and cheap, with an empirical ceiling (~100 tools) that bounds registry size.

claims.claim: Stream RAG triggers retrieval/tool queries in PARALLEL with incoming speech (before the utterance ends) over three primitives: Trigger (fixed-interval vs model-learned), Threads (parallel query streams), Reflector (are intermediate results sufficient). Fixed-interval trigger needs NO post-training; model-triggered (NO_QUERY/new-call every 500ms) needs post-training. On AudioCRAG: model-trigger 34.2% vs 11.1% baseline; latency cut 20.7% (synthetic) / 53.4% (human speech); fixed-interval gave 10.7% latency with no model update.
claims.source: Stream RAG: Instant and Accurate Spoken Dialogue Systems with Streaming Tool Usage, arXiv:2510.02044, 2025 [OPENED html]
claims.relevance: Maps 1:1 onto our Qwen3-Omni audio-in setup: fixed-interval trigger + reflector = training-free primitive; model-triggered timing = a step-3 RL lever. Newer speech-agentic entry positioned against WavRAG/SpeechRAG in our records.

claims.claim: SAGE puts a training-free NOVELTY GATE before any write-time LLM call: a von Mises-Fisher density estimator over memory embeddings routes clearly-novel->ADD, clearly-redundant->NOOP, only uncertain->LLM-merge. As a drop-in gate it skips ~16-18% of LLM calls with minimal quality change, cuts add-phase API cost 3.4x / latency 2.5x on GPT-4o-mini, and beats Mem0 token-F1 on all 7 open-weight backbones (LoCoMo).
claims.source: SAGE: A Novelty Gate for Efficient Memory Evolution in Agentic LLMs, arXiv:2605.30711, 2026 [not-opened: search-snippet]
claims.relevance: A FIXED (non-RL) write-back gate that runs purely on faiss embeddings we already compute — feasible now for our grain-tagged values, and the training-free surrogate of an RL store policy.

claims.claim: Mem0 treats memory as editable (LLM controller chooses ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP over extracted salient facts); A-Mem extends to full note-evolution rewriting linked neighbors; Agentic Memory (Yu et al. 2026) trains store/retrieve/update/summarize/discard as callable tools via a 3-stage step-wise GRPO pipeline.
claims.source: Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents survey, arXiv:2603.07670, 2026; Mem0 (Chhikara 2025); A-Mem (Xu 2025) [not-opened: search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Enumerates the write-back operation set and shows the fixed(heuristic)->LLM-judged->RL-trained ladder; the RL rung (Agentic Memory) is our out-of-mock step-3 target, the heuristic/LLM rungs are fixed-mock feasible.

claims.claim: Self-RAG's adaptive form learns four reflection-token types (Retrieve, Relevance/IsRel, Grounding/IsSup, Utility/IsUse) via a trained critic inserting tokens offline; Open-RAG extends this to a parameter-efficient sparse-MoE for harder reasoning. The adaptive reflect/verify primitive therefore REQUIRES weight training.
claims.relevance: Confirms the reflect/verify primitive's high-quality adaptive version is weight-changing (out of scope for training-free); our fixed-mock version must be a prompt-time reflection pass, and step-3 must approximate the tokens via reward, not fine-tune.

claims.claim: CRAG adds a lightweight retrieval EVALUATOR that grades retrieved docs, decomposes them into knowledge strips, and triggers corrective actions (web-search fallback / knowledge refinement) when evidence is weak; its ablation (PopQA, triggering one action for all instances) shows routing + decomposed filtering + web expansion + correctness verification each contribute non-trivially.
claims.source: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation, arXiv:2401.15884, 2024 [not-opened: search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Route+verify primitives as a fixed evaluator+threshold — feasible on our stack; the grader is the training-free surrogate for a learned relevance/grounding token.

claims.claim: Adaptive-RAG trains a T5-Large complexity classifier to route each query among three strategies (no-retrieval / single-step / multi-step), matching always-expensive baselines at substantially lower cost; SKR routes on the model's apparent self-knowledge.
claims.source: Adaptive-RAG (Jeong et al.), 2024; via A Systematic Review of RAG Systems, arXiv:2507.18910 [not-opened: search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Route/when-to-retrieve primitive with a cheap fixed classifier version (feasible) and an obvious RL-tuned-router step-3 version; three-way complexity routing is a template for our multi-store/grain routing.

claims.claim: Multi-store routing is now cast as source selection before retrieval: DeepSieve (LLM-as-knowledge-router with reflexion), R1-Router (RL, step-specific rewards to choose among multiple KBs for multimodal LLMs), RAGRouter (document + RAG-capability embeddings, contrastive), GraphRouter (link-prediction over a query-model-source graph), RealRoute (retrieve-then-verify).
claims.source: DeepSieve arXiv:2507.22050; R1-Router / Learning-to-Route arXiv:2505.22095; RAGRouter arXiv:2505.23052; RealRoute arXiv:2604.20860 [not-opened: search-snippets]
claims.relevance: Our KB has 3 explicit grains (knowledge/memory/exemplar) = a natural multi-store routing problem; a fixed heuristic/embedding router is feasible now, RL router = step-3. R1-Router is comparison-class (RL).

claims.claim: Query rewriting (Rewrite-Retrieve-Read) improves retrieval MRR ~13-14% on single-doc questions and up to +19.4pp in domain-specialized settings; ConvSearch-R1 RL-trains query reformulation for conversational search. Yet in the agentic 7B loop rewrite/decompose gains are small (~1.4 EM).
claims.source: Query Rewriting for RAG, arXiv:2305.14283, 2023; ConvSearch-R1 arXiv:2505.15776, 2025 [not-opened: search-snippets]
claims.relevance: Query-construction primitive: cheap fixed LLM-rewrite feasible; RL rewriter (ConvSearch-R1) is comparison-class. Effect is retriever-quality-dependent, small once a loop exists.

claims.claim: Reranking's value is context-dependent: with a strong reranker already present, additional retrieval enhancements add little ('Beyond the Reranker'); removing a reranker can drop answer F1 ~30pts in some cascaded pipelines, but only ~1.7 EM inside the 7B agentic loop. RL-trained rerankers exist (MM-R5, LLM-feedback-RL rerankers).
claims.source: Beyond the Reranker, arXiv:2606.28367, 2026; MM-R5 arXiv:2506.12364 [not-opened: search-snippets]
claims.relevance: Rerank primitive: high variance in payoff; on llama.cpp we'd add a separate cross-encoder or use LLM-as-reranker (extra load); worth it only if base retrieval is weak.

claims.claim: Deep-research orchestration is a plan->search->synthesize->verify pipeline with a deterministic post-processing step that verifies every citation against sources actually retrieved (auditable attribution); a separate citations agent inserts/repairs supports. Step-DeepResearch reinforces planning/gathering/reflection as atomic capabilities.
claims.source: Deep Research: A Survey of Autonomous Research Agents, arXiv:2508.12752, 2025; Step-DeepResearch arXiv:2512.20491 [not-opened: search-snippets]
claims.relevance: Verify/attribution primitive at delivery: a deterministic citation-grounding check is cheap and training-free, and is the natural home for our omni-verifier decorrelation (W4 bridge).

claims.claim: RAGCap-Bench is a capability-oriented benchmark that isolates the intermediate process-level skills of agentic RAG — reported as planning, evidence extraction, grounded reasoning, and noise robustness — and finds RAGCap performance correlates with end-to-end multi-hop QA; 'slow-thinking' models score higher, and it runs ~50x faster than full WebThinker workflows.
claims.source: RAGCap-Bench, arXiv:2510.13910, 2025 [OPENED abstract; four-capability names from search-snippet, not confirmed in abstract]
claims.relevance: Names the primitive capabilities to instrument and gives a cheap proxy to evaluate our fixed vs adaptive primitives without full end-to-end runs.

claims.claim: Online-Optimized RAG for tool use improves tool retrieval at DEPLOYMENT time via lightweight online embedding updates from live minimal feedback, with negligible per-query latency, NO change to the underlying LLM, supporting dynamic tool inventories and K-retrieval + rerank.
claims.source: Online-Optimized RAG for Tool Use and Function Calling, arXiv:2509.20415, 2025 [not-opened: search-snippet]
claims.relevance: A genuinely training-free ADAPTIVE lever (updates faiss keys, not weights) — fits our 'no weights, no structure' constraint exactly; candidate mechanism for adaptive tool/KB retrieval on speech keys.

claims.claim: The Search-R1 family — Search-R1, R1-Searcher, ReSearch, StepSearch, ZeroSearch, DeepResearcher, O2-Searcher, FrugalRAG, Tool-R1, ConvSearch-R1, R1-Router, TreePS-RAG, APEX-Searcher — all RL-train the LLM to interleave search/tool calls with reasoning (Search-R1: +41% Qwen2.5-7B, +20% 3B over RAG baselines). These change weights.
claims.source: Search-R1, arXiv:2503.09516, 2025 (+ family via search) [not-opened: search-snippets]
claims.relevance: COMPARISON CLASS, not candidates: we are training-free. Our job is to reproduce these emergent behaviors (when-to-search, decompose, verify) via inference-time reward, and to benchmark our fixed/RL-lite surrogates against this weight-training ceiling.

claims.claim: Multi-agent RAG (MA-RAG: Planner / Step-Definer / Extractor / QA agents communicating via CoT) refines retrieval+synthesis by decomposition; 'Experience as a Compass' evolves orchestration and agent prompts from accumulated experience (a training-free experience-memory form of orchestration improvement).
claims.source: MA-RAG, arXiv:2505.20096, 2025; Experience as a Compass, arXiv:2604.00901, 2026 [not-opened: search-snippets]
claims.relevance: Plan/orchestrate primitive; Experience-as-Compass shows a training-free write-back-to-orchestration path, but multiple 30B llama.cpp calls (no batching, sequential) make full multi-agent orchestration high-cost on our stack.

claims.claim: Training-free adaptive retrieval GATING from prefix logits (TARG) and forward-looking active retrieval by token-confidence (FLARE) let an off-the-shelf model decide when-to-retrieve before full decoding; unified active retrieval and uncertainty-probe variants (SeaKR, SUGAR) modulate retrieval frequency.
claims.source: TARG arXiv:2511.09803; FLARE (Jiang 2023); Unified Active Retrieval arXiv:2406.12534 [not-opened: search-snippets]
claims.relevance: The route/when-to-retrieve gate HAS a training-free version (TARG, already in our records) — so the fixed-mock gate is feasible and the step-3 lever is only a refinement, not a prerequisite.

claims.claim: Verifier-guided best-of-N / test-time selection reaches higher accuracy at lower k than self-consistency (1-3x fewer tokens); prompting-based verifiers need no training; Reason-and-Verify and FVA-RAG add faithfulness/falsification-verification passes over RAG outputs.
claims.source: Verifiers in Test-Time Scaling, arXiv:2510.25623; Reason and Verify, arXiv:2603.10143; FVA-RAG arXiv:2512.07015 [not-opened: search-snippets]
claims.relevance: This IS our W1 machinery (best-of-N + verifiable reward) applied as a RAG verify primitive; a training-free verifier-guided selection over KB-grounded candidates is our strongest, lowest-risk lever and the concrete bridge to W4 omni-verifier decorrelation.

candidates.name: Iterative retrieve-reason loop (fixed depth)
candidates.what: Alternate KB retrieval and reasoning for a FIXED small number of steps (evidence points to 2). This is the dominant primitive by ablation; a fixed depth-2 loop over our faiss KB captures ~95% of what a 5-step loop gives.
candidates.evidence: 2606.21553 (iterate -7.1 EM when removed; 2 iters=95% of 5); IRCoT/FLARE line

candidates.name: When-to-retrieve gate (training-free, TARG/FLARE-style)
candidates.what: Decide per-query/per-step whether to hit the KB at all, from prefix logits or token confidence — no weights. Fixed threshold in mock; adaptive/RL-tuned gate = step-3 lever.
candidates.evidence: TARG 2511.09803 (already in our records); FLARE; Unified Active Retrieval 2406.12534; CRAG evaluator 2401.15884

candidates.name: Multi-store / grain router
candidates.what: Route each (sub-)query to the right grain of our KB (knowledge vs memory vs exemplar) or skip. Fixed heuristic/embedding router feasible now; RL router (R1-Router) = out-of-mock step-3.

candidates.name: Query rewrite (LLM reformulation)
candidates.what: Rewrite the (possibly ASR-derived) query before retrieval to better match KB keys. Cheap fixed prompt in mock; RL rewriter (ConvSearch-R1) = comparison-class/step-3.
candidates.evidence: Rewrite-Retrieve-Read 2305.14283 (+13-14% MRR); small (-1.4 EM) inside agentic loop per 2606.21553

candidates.name: Query decomposition / sub-question planning
candidates.what: Break a multi-hop spoken question into sub-questions retrieved sequentially. Fixed decompose prompt feasible; effect modest on small models but larger in surveys/multi-agent.

candidates.name: Rerank (cross-encoder or LLM-as-reranker)
candidates.what: Reorder top-k KB hits before delivery. Payoff is high-variance: big when base retrieval is weak, ~1.7 EM inside a strong loop. On llama.cpp needs a separate reranker model or an LLM-as-reranker pass.

candidates.name: Reflect / self-critique pass (inference-time)
candidates.what: Prompt the frozen model to critique its own draft/evidence. Fixed reflection prompt is feasible but showed 'surprisingly limited' payoff on a 7B; the high-quality version (Self-RAG reflection tokens) needs weight training so is out for training-free.

candidates.name: Verify / grounding-attribution check (verifier-guided selection)
candidates.what: Generate N KB-grounded candidates and select via a verifier / faithfulness + citation-grounding check — our W1 best-of-N reward machinery reused as a RAG primitive. Training-free by construction; the omni-model-as-verifier is the W4 decorrelation bridge. Adaptive reward weighting = out-of-mock.
candidates.evidence: Verifiers in TTS 2510.25623 (fewer tokens than self-consistency); Reason-and-Verify 2603.10143; deep-research deterministic citation check 2508.12752

candidates.name: Store / write-back policy (novelty-gated)
candidates.what: Decide what to persist into the grain-tagged value store. Fixed = append-only or SAGE-style vMF novelty gate (ADD/NOOP/LLM-merge) running on faiss embeddings we already have; adaptive = Agentic-Memory RL store/update/discard policy.
candidates.evidence: SAGE 2605.30711 (training-free gate, skips 16-18% LLM calls, beats Mem0 F1); Mem0 ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP; A-Mem; Agentic Memory RL (Yu 2026)

candidates.name: Tool-registry retrieval (function calling over a tool KB)
candidates.what: Store tool/function descriptions as a KB grain and faiss-retrieve top-k per query instead of listing all tools. Fixed retrieval feasible now (directly reuses our KB); empirical ceiling ~100 tools. Adaptive = Online-Optimized RAG embedding updates (training-free) or RL selection.
candidates.evidence: RAG-MCP 2505.03275 (43.1% vs 13.6% naive, >50% token cut, degrades >100 tools); Online-Optimized RAG 2509.20415; Graph RAG-Tool Fusion 2502.07223

candidates.name: Streaming parallel trigger over speech
candidates.what: Issue KB/tool queries in parallel with the incoming audio, gated by a reflector deciding sufficiency. Fixed-interval trigger (every N ms) needs NO post-training; model-triggered timing (NO_QUERY vs call per 500ms) = step-3 RL lever. Native fit for Qwen3-Omni audio-in.
candidates.evidence: Stream RAG 2510.02044 (34.2% vs 11.1% AudioCRAG; fixed-interval 10.7% latency, no model update; model-trigger 20-53% latency)

candidates.name: Plan / multi-agent orchestration
candidates.what: Decompose the task across specialized roles (planner/extractor/QA) or a plan-then-execute pipeline. Fixed pipeline is feasible but each stage is another 30B call on a single sequential llama.cpp server, so cost is high; training-free experience-write-back to prompts (Experience-as-Compass) is a lighter variant.
candidates.evidence: MA-RAG 2505.20096; RAGCap-Bench 2510.13910 (planning is a core capability); Experience-as-Compass 2604.00901

candidates.name: Adaptive iteration-stopping / early-exit policy
candidates.what: Learn (reward-guided, training-free) when to stop the retrieve-reason loop rather than fixing depth. Given 2 iters ~= 95% of 5, the upside is small but the compute saving on a 30B is real.
candidates.evidence: 2606.21553 (diminishing returns after 2); FrugalRAG 2507.07634 (learn to retrieve fewer)

gaps: EVIDENCE GAPS (Dimension 4). (1) MODALITY TRANSFER UNMEASURED: every clean component ablation (2606.21553, RAGCap-Bench) is on TEXT 7B LLMs with text-keyed retrieval; none isolate these primitives on a FROZEN speech/omni model with a SPEECH-VECTOR-keyed KB. Whether the 'iterate dominates, route/rewrite/decompose/rerank each ~1-2 EM, verify/reflect minimal' ranking holds when keys are audio embeddings and the reasoner is Qwen3-Omni is untested — needs our own directional-only check. (2) MODEL-SCALE CONFOUND: the 'reflect/verify surprisingly limited' finding is a small-model result; a 30B omni model may benefit more from a verify/reflect pass — unresolved, and it decides whether our verifier-selection lever is worth the extra passes. (3) GRAIN-AWARE WRITE-BACK UNSTUDIED: SAGE/Mem0/A-Mem all gate a SINGLE memory store; no work routes writes across heterogeneous GRAINS (knowledge fact vs memory instance vs exemplar template) the way our value schema does — the write-policy for a multi-grain store is open. (4) TRAINING-FREE-ADAPTIVE COUNTERPARTS UNDER-BENCHMARKED: nearly every adaptive primitive in 2025-26 is RL-trained (Search-R1 family, R1-Router, Agentic-Memory RL, MM-R5, ConvSearch-R1); the training-free surrogate of each (fixed threshold / prompt / heuristic / online-embedding-update) is rarely ablated against its RL version, so which fixed surrogate best approximates each learned primitive is unknown — this is exactly the question our program must answer. (5) ONLINE-EMBEDDING-UPDATE ON SPEECH KEYS UNPROVEN: Online-Optimized RAG (2509.20415) is the cleanest 'no-weights' adaptive retrieval lever but is demonstrated on text tool inventories, not speech-keyed KBs. (6) VERIFIER-SELECTION AS A RAG PRIMITIVE lacks a clean training-free-vs-RL ablation grounded in KB retrieval, despite being our W1/W4 bridge. (7) STACK-COST BLINDSPOT: no latency/throughput study of running route+rerank+verify+reflect all on a SINGLE sequential llama.cpp 30B server (no batching); multi-agent orchestration cost on this exact hardware is unquantified and may dominate the primitive-selection decision.
